text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--- The government has postponed public building projects worth 530 million crowns to avoid exacerbating a shortage of construction tradesmen.
--- The number of Danes who have died from alcohol abuse related diseases has more than trebled over the past 24 years from 8.7 per thousand in 1970 to 29.5 per thousand in 1994.
--- 60 percent of voters want to revoke the Danish optout on police cooperation introduced when Denmark voted in favour of the European Union Maastricht treaty in 1993, a new survey shows.
--- Danish exports are facing difficulties, but Denmark will be able to maintain its balance of payments surplus in spite of this, finance minister Mogens Lykketoft says.

--- The European Commission warns that inflation will harm Denmark's competitiveness, in its yearly report on the 15 European Union counties' economies, but finance minister Mogens Lykketoft says that there is no need to panic.
--- Copenhagen needs a congress centre and more international hotels to attract wealthy culture and business tourists, but investors are not interested.

--- Danish pork producers want food minister Henrik Dam Kristensen to prevent the spread of swine disease from the Netherlands and Germany by interoducing stricter control of trucks driving livestock across the Danish-German border.
